meta.title: The Big Turnip
meta.textType: story: a traditional story with repeated lines

paragraphs: Every month, Lily and Tom travel to Green Hill by bus. Green Hill is a small village near the town. One Saturday, Grandpa showed them a big turnip in his garden. It was too big for one person. Grandma was in the kitchen, and the house smelled of rice. "Do you know the story of the big turnip?" asked Grandpa. "No," said Lily. "Pull with your hands when you hear the words," said Grandpa.

A man planted a small turnip, and it grew very big. "Pull, pull, pull!" said the man. But the turnip did not come off the ground. The man called his wife. The wife pulled the man, and the man pulled the turnip. "Pull, pull, pull!" they said. But the turnip did not come off the ground. Lily and Tom pulled with their hands, and they all laughed together.

Next, a girl pulled the wife, and the dog pulled the girl. The cat pulled the dog. "Pull, pull, pull!" they said. But the turnip did not come off the ground. Last, a little mouse pulled the cat. "Pull, pull, pull!" they said. The turnip came off the ground at last! Then everyone fell down in the garden. Everyone was tired, but happy.

After the story, Grandma cooked a small turnip with a red sauce and some salt. The sauce was sweet and a little hot. Everyone ate the turnip with a fork. "The mouse was small," said Grandpa, "but the mouse was important." "Every helper is important." Tom smiled and said, "I will help with the next turnip." Tom and Lily were important too.
text.summary: Grandpa tells Lily and Tom the story of a big turnip. Many helpers pull it, and the smallest helper is important too.
